fields.name: motion_reference
fields.description: With empty memory write [E0]. If the incoming list contains only E0 and this cycle shows that execution time has advanced, append all displayed execution front-camera labels in chronological order, excluding duplicates. Otherwise carry the incoming list unchanged. A zero-step action does not trigger appending. Once the initial motion frames have been appended, never append further frames or replace the list. Use the stored images and their absolute step labels as the reference for reconstructing the cube's periodic motion. e.g. ["E0", "E1", "E17", "E33", "E46"]
fields.annotation: An ordered list of execution keyframes documenting the initial cube motion. At the first cycle write [E0]. At the first cycle showing actual elapsed motion, append that cycle's displayed front-camera frame labels in chronological order, excluding duplicates. Freeze this list thereafter. These frames preserve the initial endpoint, early motion and its absolute timing, allowing the oscillation period and numbered future target passages to be inferred even when later images show the same positions again. They also retain the unobstructed button location. Do not select frames from future cycles. e.g. ["E0", "E1", "E17", "E33", "E46"]

action:
Start by locating the gray circular button on its white base, the colored moving cube, and the purple target. Infer the button's world xy from the calibrated images and its tabletop base, using the wrist view to refine localization. Do not use image left/right as robot left/right. When the TCP is initially high and has not approached the button, command [button_x, button_y, 0.15, -3.1416, 0, 0] with gripper command -1. Use the button center, not the slightly displaced achieved hover TCP, for subsequent commanded xy.

While hovering approximately 0.15 m above the button, keep the gripper closed and determine when to press. Read the requested ordinal N from the goal. Use motion_reference together with the current motion frames and absolute elapsed_control_steps to reconstruct the cube's oscillation. The cube starts at one endpoint and moves smoothly back and forth; count a passage through the target in either direction, not a complete round trip. Fit the motion in world tabletop coordinates rather than assuming constant image velocity. In these trajectories the target is the midpoint of the oscillation: for full period P, passage times are P/4 + (N-1)P/2. Infer P from observed motion, not from the requested ordinal or the cube's color. The demonstrated periods include 120, 160 and 240 control steps. Initial and current frames should agree with the inferred phase; do not reset the passage count when the cube returns to an earlier-looking position.

Begin the downward press about 20 control steps before the requested target passage. Thus compute the press-start step S = P/4 + (N-1)P/2 - L. Use L = 20 steps normally; use approximately 22 steps for a button toward the robot's far right, near y = -0.19 m, where the demonstrated descent needs slightly more lead. This gives press starts of 400 for the fourth passage with P=240, 280 for the third with P=240, 190 for the fourth with P=120, approximately 178 for the third with P=160 at the far-right button, and 340 for the fifth with P=160. These are consequences of measured periods and button geometry, not episode identifiers.

If the current step t is below S, wait min(30, round(S-t)) control steps in place, maintaining the closed gripper. Do not take an extra full 30-step wait when fewer steps remain. If t has reached S and the hand is still hovering, command [button_x, button_y, 0.0075, -3.1416, 0, 0] with gripper command -1. The press waypoint is intentionally below the contact-limited achieved TCP height; do not substitute the observed contact height for the command. Account for motion time: waiting until the cube visibly reaches the target before starting the descent is too late.

If the TCP is down at the button, approximately z=0.025 m, following a visible descent and contact, retract to [button_x, button_y, 0.15, -3.1416, 0, 0], keeping the gripper closed. Do not press again simply because the cube remains near the target. A stopped cube after contact calls for retraction or, if already retracted, a short wait for termination.

If observations do not support a reliable period, compare retained initial motion with the current frames and wait a short interval, at most 10 steps, to disambiguate direction and speed rather than pressing on an uncertain passage. If the button is temporarily occluded, recover its position from the retained unobstructed frames. If alignment is genuinely lost, move to the safe button-centered hover before attempting contact. Never issue an identical-pose waypoint; use a wait when no movement is needed.
